label: Subject dependence in the focal-role candidate
definition: Inheres x s means that x depends on s as its subject: e.g. this particular color inheres in this colored thing, under a selected substance/accident framework. It does not mean spatial inclusion, parthood, predicating a species, productive causation or divine creation. A painter producing pigment, a part in a whole, or one independent stone next to another is not by that fact an inherence edge. Substance and existence remain explicitly supplied predicates. Substance is itself a supplied primitive classification of represented individual bearers rather than their dependent features (e.g. a stone as bearer, not its particular color); this candidate does not define substance by self-causing, Godhood or necessary existence. Exists is an independent one-world valuation, not automatically membership of the carrier.
note: The parameter Inheres is primitive, not a completed reduction of dependence; Secondary defines the existential subject-linked account around it. SubjectFocalReading explicitly requires existent dependents, substantial existent subjects, nonsubstantial dependents and distinctness. No transitivity, temporal dependence, persistence or modal inability to exist apart is assumed. Under this candidate edges cannot cycle since a dependent is not substantial and its subject is substantial. Applicability to reality, substance individuation, and stronger existential/modal dependence remain OPEN. Bundle theory, trope theory and accounts rejecting accidents are live rivals; finite witnesses do not refute them. Categories.PrimarySubstanceBySubjectRelationsReading intentionally leaves its In relation unspecified and is not identified with this one. See docs/being-not-a-genus.md, Subject focal-role candidate.
